subject.title: feat(queue): persist followup queues across gateway restarts

question: Should restored follow-up queues promise exactly-once delivery across a crash between channel send and SQLite acknowledgement, or should this feature explicitly provide at-least-once recovery?
rationale: A shared SQLite queue cannot atomically commit an external channel side effect, so the desired semantics determine whether the current acknowledgement pattern is acceptable or a broader idempotency design is required.

options.title: Define at-least-once recovery
options.body: Keep the bounded SQLite persistence design, remove the exactly-once claim, and document/test the possible duplicate after a crash during acknowledgement.

options.title: Require exactly-once semantics
options.body: Pause this branch for a delivery-idempotency design that lets supported channels recognize a recovered item already sent before the crash.

options.title: Defer restart persistence
options.body: Keep current in-memory behavior until the delivery contract can be designed across channel ownership boundaries.

recommendation.title: Define at-least-once recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded SQLite persistence design, remove the exactly-once claim, and document/test the possible duplicate after a crash during acknowledgement.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent queue-state history most directly connects this person to the state and draining boundary where the delivery contract must be chosen.
